questions: How do the three products fit together?
entries.answer: GQ Studio is the single application shell over the whole platform: the workspaces, screens, and low-code customization layer that tie GQData, GQ Govern, and GQ Agents into one product experience. It is where data engineers, stewards, compliance officers, and AI engineers all work on the same records against the same trail. It ships with the platform rather than being sold on its own.

questions: Tell me about your GST product
Do you have anything for Indian tax?
What does the GST co-pilot actually do?
entries.answer: GST Co-Pilot is a four-agent system for Indian GST work: invoice ingestion, extraction, GSTR-2B reconciliation, and exception resolution. An orchestrator reads intent, routes work, and escalates to a human reviewer above a configurable threshold. It compresses the forty-plus hours a month an average mid-market tax team spends on manual reconciliation into an afternoon, and it is our reference architecture for governed agentic AI in production.

questions: How do you match invoices to GSTR-2B?
What if the invoice number is formatted differently?
entries.answer: Five passes, each less strict than the last, and each one works only on what earlier passes left behind. Pass one matches the e-invoice IRN at full confidence. Pass two matches GSTIN plus a normalised invoice number and value within a rupee. Pass three allows a fuzzy invoice number. Pass four uses amount and date. Pass five is amount only and always goes to a reviewer.

questions: What happens when an invoice is missing from GSTR-2B?
How do you handle ITC risk?
What if my vendor has not filed?
entries.answer: Your purchase register is compared against the GSTR-2B the portal publishes from vendor filings. Anything still unmatched is checked against adjacent periods first, since late filing is common, then classified as missing in GSTR-2B or missing in books. Each one is scored zero to a hundred for ITC risk and given a priority and an SLA, so critical items reach the finance team first.

questions: Tell me about the Champ agent swarm
Do you use AI to build software?
How does the agent swarm work?
entries.answer: Champ is our peer-based agent swarm for end-to-end software delivery. Agents talk through work packets on a shared board, with no hierarchy. Champ decomposes a PRD into packets, dispatches them, and watches progress. Specialist agents cover architecture, development, QA, PR review, and deployment, several running their own mini-swarms. Every packet carries a unique id, a phase history, and an append-only event log entry.

questions: How do you test your agents?
How do you know an agent actually did the work?
How are agents verified before deployment?
Do you keep auditing agents after launch?
entries.answer: An agent reporting done has told you about its confidence. So every result passes through a harness the agent does not control: it works in a sealed sandbox with a written brief and a time budget, then a separate grader inspects the artefacts it left and returns pass or fail. Before a check ships, a do-nothing agent has to fail it and a correct answer has to pass it.

questions: Do you have a retail product?
entries.answer: Commerce Synapse is our retail and commerce vertical product: AI-orchestrated commerce operations on a trusted product and customer foundation, so operations, pricing, and merchandising decisions all run on unified data. Like GST Co-Pilot, it is a reference architecture for governed agentic AI in a real domain, built on the Greyquill platform. It lives at its own address, linked from the products page.

questions: Tell me about your health platform
entries.answer: Umami is our healthcare vertical product: AI-powered practice management for medical clinics, with audit trails and clinical-workflow controls built in. The Document Center publishes its data model, which maps real-world concepts like doctor, nurse, and hospital onto a FHIR-aligned entity model organised by domain. We have shipped in healthcare, though we do not claim deep references in that vertical yet.

questions: How do I score an AI initiative?
entries.answer: ClarityAI scores the clarity and risk of an initiative before you fund it. Drop in a PRD, AI brief, RFP, or statement of work as PDF, DOCX, or plain text and it returns a clarity score, line-by-line fixes, and a one-page go, hold, or kill summary. It scores ambiguity, testability, edge-case coverage, regulatory exposure, and dependency risk. It works standalone, with no signup.

questions: What does your digital transformation service cover?
Can you modernise our old systems?
How do you handle a legacy rewrite?
entries.answer: We modernise the systems you already run, step by step. Map the estate, pick one seam with a small blast radius, build alongside it behind a clean interface, run old and new against the same work until the numbers reconcile, then retire the legacy piece and repeat. That covers legacy application modernisation, process automation, systems and data integration, and cloud migration. No big-bang rewrites.

questions: What does your AI and data service cover?
Do you run AI training or workshops?
Where should we start with AI?
entries.answer: Twelve engagements across training, assessments, and consulting, organised in five phases from boardroom to production: Align, Diagnose, Plan, Build, Ship. Most clients start at Phase 01 and can stop at any milestone. The later phases are build phases run by the same engineers who build the platform, covering LLM applications and retrieval, agentic systems, master data and lineage, and evaluation and monitoring.

questions: What does your product engineering service cover?
Can you add AI features to our existing product?
entries.answer: Discovery to design to production, with one senior team owning the outcome. Discovery and scoping workshops, UX and product design, web, mobile, and backend engineering, AI-native features that ship with evaluation, guardrails, and an audit trail, QA and reliability, then DevOps. Every brief runs through ClarityAI first. After launch we can stay on as the product team, and everything is yours to own.

questions: What have you done in BFSI?
entries.answer: Banking, financial services, and payments, where AI lives or dies on auditability. We have built a multi-rail payment processing layer handling tens of thousands of transactions per minute, and a reconciliation engine with rule-based first-pass matching, ML-assisted fuzzy matching, and a human review queue carrying lineage on every decision. The regulatory ground includes RBI, SEBI, DPDP, FCA, PRA, FFIEC, OCC, PCI-DSS, and Basel III.

questions: What have you done in telecom?
Can you help modernise a telecom platform?
Do you do churn or agent assist?
entries.answer: Telecom estates carry decades of legacy and customer data spread across a dozen systems. We have retired pieces of an aging platform module by module while the business kept running, built a master-data layer unifying customer identity across CRM, billing, and OSS, and replaced brittle RPA scripts with multi-agent orchestrations that ask a human when uncertain. Identity gets reconciled before any model is allowed to act.

questions: What have you done for retailers?
Can you help with dashboard sprawl?
entries.answer: Retail decisions repeat daily across millions of SKUs and customers. We have mapped and simplified overlapping operational workflows at a retailer that grew by acquisition, consolidated dozens of conflicting dashboards into one decision surface on a governed data layer, and fused point-of-sale, e-commerce, and supplier signals with lineage under ML-assisted demand forecasting. Consolidation usually beats new analytics.

questions: How long does a project take?
How quickly can we see something?
How long until we go live?
entries.answer: It depends on scope and complexity. A typical custom build runs three to six months from discovery to deployment, and smaller assessments or training engagements run in weeks. On the platform we aim at one governed entity serving through the API as the first milestone, because that proves the whole chain end to end. You get a specific timeline at the end of discovery.

We do not publish rates. Quotes are scoped after discovery, with defined payment milestones, itemised invoices, and no hidden fees, and pricing is value-based against the business outcome. Use the contact form and pick Request a quote, with enough detail about the project for us to give a meaningful estimate. We are also upfront that we are not the cheapest option.

questions: Do you support what you build?
entries.answer: Yes. We walk alongside clients through the operating life of the software, and most of our work is repeat work. Options include maintenance agreements, enhancement work, and training so your team can run the system on their own. Every engagement carries defined SLAs for issue response and resolution, regular maintenance and security updates, multiple support channels, and a warranty period on what we deliver.

questions: Will your security team talk to ours?
entries.answer: Security and privacy are built into every engagement. We follow secure development practices, encrypt sensitive data, and align with the regulations relevant to your jurisdiction, including GDPR, DPDP, CCPA, and PCI-DSS. The platform installs into your own environment, so records, lineage, and the audit trail never cross our boundary, and authentication runs through your own identity provider over OAuth2 and OIDC.

We are a Silver-tier IBM Partner Plus member, and our engineers hold current certifications across the stack we ship on: watsonx.ai, watsonx.data, watsonx.data intelligence, watsonx.data integration, watsonx.governance, IBM Verify, and IBM Business Automation. On frameworks like SOC 2 and ISO 27001, GQ Govern checks controls against them for you. Bring your own audit requirements and we will answer them directly.

questions: Which compliance frameworks do you support?
Do you cover the EU AI Act?
What standards can you check against?
entries.answer: Five standards are checkable today in GQ Govern: the EU AI Act, GDPR, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and India's DPDP Act, with dozens more mapped by domain and region so a workspace can find the one it actually needs. Each pass names the policy enforcing it, and a miss becomes a documented exception with a reason, a compensating action, a target date, and a named approver.

questions: Can you work with our existing systems?
Will this integrate with our legacy core?
Does this replace our data warehouse?
Do we have to rip anything out?
entries.answer: Yes. Most of what we build layers onto existing estates: legacy core systems, OSS/BSS, ERPs, data warehouses, and identity providers. Where a legacy system cannot change, we put an API facade in front of it and move data over event-driven pipelines. GQ Studio sits alongside your warehouse or lake, reading from your systems of record and serving governed entities out.

questions: Tell me about the IBM partnership
What does built on IBM foundations mean?
entries.answer: We are a Silver-tier IBM Partner Plus member, certified across watsonx and IBM Verify. We chose that foundation because watsonx carries lineage, model governance, and audit primitives risk and compliance teams already recognise, which is less work to defend. Your data, governance configuration, and agent definitions stay yours. We use the IBM stack where it earns its place and compose with other systems where they are stronger.

We are an enterprise AI consulting firm and an IBM Business Partner based in Bengaluru, working with regulated organisations across banking, insurance, retail, and telecom. Four founding engineers cover architecture, business analysis, infrastructure, and design, backed by a wider delivery team, with fifty-plus years of combined experience shipping enterprise software in regulated sectors. We are a consulting firm as much as a product team, and at this stage that matters.

We install into your environment: your cloud account, your region, your identity provider, your keys. The major clouds are supported and the pattern is the same on each, with on-prem and air-gapped topologies covered in the architecture brief. Containers run on Red Hat OpenShift with namespace-per-tenant isolation. Every source is residency-checked when it is connected, then enforced on every read after that.

questions: Do you have an architecture document?
Can I get something for my CISO?
What can I share with InfoSec?
entries.answer: Yes. The architecture and governance brief runs two to three pages, written for whoever inside your organisation approves this before procurement signs. It covers deployment topology across your cloud, on-prem, or air-gapped, data residency, the IBM stack components used and which are replaceable, identity and SSO with your own IdP, audit evidence flow, and what you take with you when the engagement ends.

questions: Where can I read more technical detail?
entries.answer: The Document Center is a curated space for open Greyquill material. It carries the GQ Studio product preview, platform and architecture documents including the C4 model and the GQ Data build explainer, five method documents on how we build, four on the Champ agent swarm, five on GST Co-Pilot's architecture and engine, and the FHIR-aligned healthcare data model. Every method page has a one-page PDF summary.

questions: How do you replace a legacy system safely?
How do you avoid a big-bang rewrite?
How do you prove the new system is right?
entries.answer: It is how we replace a legacy system without a big-bang rewrite. Pick a seam, build the replacement behind a facade, then have both process the same real work and classify every difference: a match, a tolerable difference, a defect in the replacement, or a defect in the legacy that has run for years. You cut over once real divergences hold at zero across a full business cycle.

questions: How do you map a legacy estate?
Where do you start with modernisation?
How do you find undocumented dependencies?
Do we need a discovery tool for that?
entries.answer: Before touching a legacy estate we write down what actually exists: six columns per system, covering every inbound and outbound path including manual uploads, email attachments, and someone rekeying from a screen. Interviews miss the systems nobody has thought about in years, so we also read firewall and DNS config, scheduled jobs, and database accounts. A filled-in spreadsheet beats a discovery platform nobody has populated.

questions: How do you decide what to automate?
When does a human stay in the loop?
How do you set a confidence threshold?
entries.answer: Map the process first, then sort each step: deterministic steps become plain software, judgement steps get agents, and some steps stay with a person. Judgement steps get a confidence line, and everything below it goes to review. Start with a shadow period where everything is reviewed, read the agreement rate by confidence band, set the line, then move it on evidence with a named approver and a date.

questions: What do we get out of discovery?
entries.answer: Five days of structured questioning that turn an idea into something a team can build from and a sponsor can fund. Day one fixes the outcome and how anyone would know it landed. Day two walks the workflow end to end with the people who perform it. Day three collects constraints, day four weighs at least two routes, day five sets scope, order, and estimate.

questions: When is an AI feature done?
What is your definition of done for AI?
How do you test AI features?
What gates does an AI feature pass?
entries.answer: A normal definition of done assumes a feature passing today will pass tomorrow, and a model breaks that. So we gate on an evaluation set written before the build finished, a grader proven to fail a wrong answer, repeated runs with the spread recorded, a test that attempts each guardrail, an exercised failure path, and a record of every decision. Cost and latency at peak are advisory gates.

questions: What happens if we stop working with you?
Can we take our data out?
What do we keep at the end?
entries.answer: You keep everything. Clients receive full ownership of custom-developed code on completion, and golden records, lineage, and the full audit trail export in open formats whenever you ask for them. Your governance configuration and agent definitions are yours as well. Open standards run across the stack, so the evidence belongs to you rather than being something you rent from us.

questions: Do you have anything for my industry?
How do you adapt to a new domain?
Can we bring our own data model?
entries.answer: The platform underneath is the same everywhere. What changes by industry is the pack: the entity model, the survivorship defaults, the control set, and the workflows you start from. A pack is configuration rather than a fork, so you keep getting platform improvements as they land, and a new industry means writing a new pack with no change to the engine. Insurance claims is the first one.

questions: Which languages do you work in?
entries.answer: Go, Python, JavaScript and TypeScript, with React, Next.js and Node.js on the web, and Flutter or React Native on mobile. PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB and Redis for data. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and IBM Cloud for hosting. Jenkins, CircleCI, GitHub Actions, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform and Ansible for delivery. That is the shortlist rather than the limit, so ask about yours.

We are early, so there are no logos or testimonials yet. Customer names stay withheld, though the patterns are real: a multi-rail payments platform, a telecom modernisation carried out while the platform stayed in production, retail process and reporting consolidation. GQ Studio is in product preview with a small number of design partners. If you want a reference before signing, we may not have one and will say so.
